chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq, from Sa'dan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
It is befitting for the neighbours of the bereaved that they should feed him food for three days.
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended social duty of neighbours towards a bereaved family in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), establishing the three-day meal provision by neighbors as a recommended social etiquette (adab) to alleviate the burden of cooking on the bereaved. This practice reflects the deep communal solidarity (ta'awun) emphasized in Shia tradition, particularly highlighted during the mourning of Imam al-Husayn (AS), where neighbors collectively support the family in their grief.
